doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

title: Defining swing and the primacy of the beat
summary: Swing is everything clicking; Beal says all music is about the beat and a conductor with the beat can survive.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Can you define swing? What a question, ey?
Can I define swing? Swing is when everything is clicking and it’s intense and it feels good. What can I say? Everybody’s on the same plane.

Exactly. And I think it has something to do as well as like the volume balance between the rhythm section instruments ‘cause when you think about Basie’s classic rhythm section it sounded like one instrument almost, everything is just so in sync. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Yeah, it’s all about the beat, man. And all music is about the beat. And a conductor that has the beat is usually a good conductor you know. And he doesn’t even have to read music, if he’s got the beat he can survive. I’ve worked with conductors like that.
Wow. You mean that they didn’t really — weren’t reading the score?
Right. The ear you know. And the ear determines pitch too you know, it’s not just pressing the buttons you know. You adjust. But the beat is primary.
